es.summary: Trastorno del estado de ánimo que produce tristeza persistente, pérdida de interés y deterioro funcional durante al menos dos semanas.
key_points: Diagnóstico clínico basado en criterios DSM-5 y escalas como PHQ‑9.
Tipos principales: depresión mayor y trastorno depresivo persistente.
Tratamiento multimodal: psicoterapia + antidepresivos (ISRS, IRSN, TCA).
Riesgo de suicidio y de deterioro de la adherencia al tratamiento.
Importancia de la evaluación de factores psicosociales y comorbilidades médicas.

pathophysiology: Disfunción del eje HPA con aumento de cortisol.
Cambios neuroplásticos y reducción del volumen hipocampal.
Inflamación sistémica y aumento de citocinas proinflamatorias.
risk_factors: Abuso de sustancias y consumo de alcohol.
signs_symptoms: Estado de ánimo deprimido la mayor parte del día.
Pérdida de interés o placer en actividades habituales.
Fatiga, pérdida o aumento de peso sin causa aparente.
Sentimientos de culpa, inutilidad o pensamientos suicidas.
diagnostics: Escala PHQ‑9: puntuación ≥10 sugiere depresión moderada‑grave.
Exámenes de laboratorio básicos (glucosa, TSH, hemograma) para descartar causas orgánicas.
Evaluación de riesgo suicida mediante preguntas directas.
treatment: Educación sobre adherencia y efectos adversos (náuseas, insomnio, disfunción sexual).
Intervención de crisis y plan de seguridad para riesgo suicida.
nursing_care: Evaluar humor, sueño, apetito y nivel de energía en cada turno.
Monitorear signos de suicidio: planes, intentos previos, cambios de comportamiento.
Administrar antidepresivos según prescripción y observar efectos adversos.
Facilitar ambiente seguro, retirar objetos potencialmente peligrosos.
Fomentar apoyo social y derivar a trabajo social o psicología cuando sea necesario.
patient_teaching: Importancia de tomar la medicación diariamente aunque los síntomas mejoren.
Posibles efectos secundarios y cuándo reportarlos al profesional.
Estrategias de autocuidado: ejercicio regular, higiene del sueño y alimentación balanceada.
Señalar recursos de apoyo (líneas de ayuda, grupos de apoyo).
Plan de seguridad: quién contactar en caso de pensamientos suicidas.

outcomes: Reducción de la ansiedad: puntuación en escala de ansiedad ≤5 en 2 semanas
Mejora del sueño: dormir ≥6 horas continuas por noche

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de ansiedad usando escala de Hamilton cada 24 h
interventions.rationale: Permite cuantificar la respuesta al tratamiento y ajustar intervenciones

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de respiración diafragmática y relajación muscular progresiva
interventions.rationale: Disminuye la activación fisiológica asociada a la ansiedad

interventions.action: Proveer un ambiente tranquilo, reducir estímulos ruidosos y luz intensa
interventions.rationale: Minimiza factores que exacerban la ansiedad

interventions.action: Administrar antidepresivo ISRS según prescripción y observar efectos adversos
interventions.rationale: Los ISRS reducen la ansiedad al modular serotonina

interventions.action: Facilitar contacto con familia o grupo de apoyo
interventions.rationale: El apoyo social es protector contra la ansiedad

outcomes: Demostrar uso de al menos 2 estrategias de afrontamiento adaptativo en 1 semana
Participar en actividades de autocuidado al menos 3 veces por semana

interventions.action: Evaluar habilidades de afrontamiento mediante entrevista estructurada
interventions.rationale: Identifica áreas específicas que requieren refuerzo

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de solución de problemas y reestructuración cognitiva
interventions.rationale: Promueve respuestas más efectivas ante situaciones estresantes

interventions.action: Fomentar la elaboración de un plan de actividades diarias realista
interventions.rationale: Restablece la rutina y mejora la sensación de control

interventions.action: Derivar a terapia grupal o individual según disponibilidad
interventions.rationale: La terapia brinda apoyo profesional para desarrollar habilidades de afrontamiento

interventions.action: Monitorear adherencia al tratamiento farmacológico y registrar efectos secundarios
interventions.rationale: Asegura que la medicación contribuya al mejoramiento del estado de ánimo

en.summary: Mood disorder that produces persistent sadness, loss of interest and functional impairment for at least two weeks.
key_points: Clinical diagnosis based on DSM‑5 criteria and scales such as PHQ‑9.
Main types: Major Depressive Disorder and Persistent Depressive Disorder.
Multimodal treatment: psychotherapy + antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs).
Risk of suicide and treatment adherence deterioration.
Importance of evaluating psychosocial factors and medical comorbidities.

pathophysiology: HPA axis dysfunction with increased cortisol.
Neuroplastic changes and reduced hippocampal volume.
Systemic inflammation and increased pro‑inflammatory cytokines.
signs_symptoms: Depressed mood most of the day.
Loss of interest or pleasure in usual activities.
Fatigue, unexplained weight loss or gain.
Feelings of guilt, worthlessness or suicidal thoughts.
diagnostics: Basic labs (glucose, TSH, CBC) to rule out organic causes.
Suicide risk assessment with direct questioning.
treatment: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) or Interpersonal Therapy.
Education on adherence and side effects (nausea, insomnia, sexual dysfunction).
Crisis intervention and safety plan for suicide risk.
nursing_care: Assess mood, sleep, appetite, and energy level each shift.
Monitor suicide signs: plans, prior attempts, behavior changes.
Administer antidepressants per prescription and monitor adverse effects.
Create a safe environment, remove potentially dangerous objects.
Encourage social support and refer to social work or psychology when needed.
patient_teaching: Importance of taking medication daily even if symptoms improve.
Possible side effects and when to report them to the provider.
Self‑care strategies: regular exercise, sleep hygiene, balanced diet.
Safety plan: who to contact if suicidal thoughts arise.

outcomes: Reduction of anxiety: anxiety scale score ≤5 in 2 weeks
Improved sleep: sleep ≥6 continuous hours per night

interventions.action: Assess anxiety level using Hamilton scale every 24 h
interventions.rationale: Allows quantifying treatment response and adjusting interventions

interventions.action: Teach diaphragmatic breathing and progressive muscle relaxation
interventions.rationale: Reduces physiological activation associated with anxiety

interventions.action: Provide a calm environment, reduce loud stimuli and intense light
interventions.rationale: Minimizes factors that exacerbate anxiety

interventions.action: Administer SSRI antidepressant per prescription and monitor adverse effects
interventions.rationale: SSRIs reduce anxiety by modulating serotonin

interventions.action: Facilitate contact with family or support group
interventions.rationale: Social support protects against anxiety

outcomes: Demonstrate use of at least 2 adaptive coping strategies in 1 week
Participate in self‑care activities at least 3 times per week

interventions.action: Assess coping skills via structured interview
interventions.rationale: Identifies specific areas needing reinforcement

interventions.action: Teach problem‑solving and cognitive restructuring techniques
interventions.rationale: Promotes more effective responses to stressful situations

interventions.action: Encourage development of a realistic daily activity plan
interventions.rationale: Restores routine and improves sense of control

interventions.action: Refer to group or individual therapy as available
interventions.rationale: Therapy provides professional support to develop coping skills

interventions.action: Monitor medication adherence and record side effects
interventions.rationale: Ensures medication contributes to mood improvement

sources.name: Maternal-Newborn Nursing: Postpartum Mood Disorders and Psychiatric Disorders

summary.0.quote: Major depression symptoms include a depressed mood or a loss of interest. Symptoms affect your daily activities and last for at least two weeks.

key_points.1.quote: The most common types of depression are major depression and persistent depressive disorder.

key_points.2.quote: Most treatments include medicines and/or psychotherapy (talk therapy): Medicines such as antidepressants may help control your symptoms.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Vortioxetine: Increases the release of several neurotransmitters (serotonin, NE, dopamine, glutamate, acetylcholine, and histamine).

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: A medical history will include asking about your symptoms and family history.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Going through trauma or stressful life events may raise your risk even more.

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: Other mental disorders or chronic medical conditions such as diabetes , cancer , or heart disease may occur with depression.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: At least one of the symptoms is either depressed mood most of the day nearly every day or loss of interest or pleasure.

sections.complications.0.quote: When the nurse recognizes signs of PPD, the nurse diagnoses ineffective coping, impaired bonding, risk for impaired parenting, and risk for self-harm.
